extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media researchers, health news consumers, and public relations professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used to evaluate the completeness, accuracy, and balance of news stories (and later PR news releases) that make claims about medical treatments, tests, products, and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Rated the completeness of news stories that include claims about medical treatments, tests, products and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the site's overall evaluation focus (along with accuracy and balance). The site's reviews assessed whether stories included necessary contextual information to be considered complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rated the accuracy of news stories that include claims about medical treatments, tests, products and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates factual correctness of claims made in the story as part of the site's 10-point grading approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rated the balance of news stories that include claims about medical treatments, tests, products and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether reporting presented competing viewpoints or acknowledged uncertainty rather than presenting one-sided conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides information about sources and their competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story gives information about its sources and their competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly listed among items in the project's 10-point grading scale; disclosure of sources' conflicts is required to judge potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifies the benefits of a treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story quantifies the benefits of a treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the 10-point grading scale; evaluation emphasizes numeric quantification (not just qualitative claims) to allow readers to judge effect size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraises the evidence supporting the story's claims / discusses evidence quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story appraises the evidence supporting the story's claims and discusses the quality of that evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site found many stories 'failed to discuss evidence quality.' Appraising evidence quality is central to determining whether claims are well-supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discusses alternative options
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story discusses alternative options (other treatments or approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noting alternatives helps contextualize a treatment's relative value; the site reported many stories failed to discuss alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discusses costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story discusses costs related to the treatment, test, product, or procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of costs is part of providing complete information for readers; the site observed cost discussion was often missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides absolute sizes of benefits and harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story reports the absolute sizes of benefits and harms (not just relative or vague claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site specifically flagged absence of 'absolute sizes of benefits and harms' as a common failing; conveying absolute risks/benefits is important for accurate public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10-point grading scale (meta-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The project used a 10-point grading scale that included items such as disclosure of sources and competing interests, quantification of benefits, and appraisal of supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the formal scoring framework for reviews; individual items in the scale map to the specific criteria listed above. The scale was later applied both to news stories and (from 2015) to health care PR news releases.
